P22a: The Amish let their young people make the decision to join the church on their own when they're adults, and roughly 85 percent or more of them end up joining. The whole Rumspringa thing gets blown out of proportion in popular culture, as if every teenager went wild. Still, it matters that they're baptized as adults and not as infants, because that makes belonging a commitment instead of a fact imposed at birth.
P22b: The Amish let their young people make the decision to join the church on their own when they're adults, and roughly 85 percent or more of them end up joining. Pop culture blows Rumspringa way out of proportion, as if every teenager went wild. But they're still baptized as adults, not as kids, and that makes belonging a commitment instead of a fact imposed at birth.
P24b: Every childhood narrows the future. Most ordinary parents aren't going to give their kid a bunch of money at 18 and say, "Go see the world." They'll try to get them ready for some next step that can actually work. A poor or money-free community may have even less cash to go around, and food, medical care and basic survival may rightly come first.
